For nonresonant targets the two nonzero limiting cubic boundaries shift by O(R^{-1}) in rescaled x, yielding an O(1)-width boundary layer and a middle strip on which each full cosine half-period contains exactly one simple root. Curvature/derivative control bounds all edge roots uniformly, yielding an all-root O(1) counting error. Root-grid coupling gives the W1 rate; finite checker tests only algebraic identities and examples.

value.rationale: The weak-coupling limit beta→0 is an intrinsic decoupling boundary of an established fixed-point-free dynamical family. The finding quantifies a genuinely singular finite-to-infinite inverse-fiber transition, including target-dependent beta^{-1/3} coefficient, uniform rescaled preimage distribution, and exact signed cancellation at fixed degree +1. It applies to entire compact target families on both sides of the limiting image and is not a routine finite sample or short-cycle reformulation.
